Ux1lwW-Jxlo.title: Contemporary Issues: Climate Change
Ux1lwW-Jxlo.one_line: Stewardship of the earth makes climate change a first-tier justice issue for Muslims in the West, with four practical steps.
Ux1lwW-Jxlo.summary: He opens with the first verse after the introduction of Al-Baqarah, where Allah declares He will place a steward on earth, and corrects the idea that Adam was meant to stay in paradise: humans were created for stewardship of this earth, and that is how they serve Allah until the earth is gone. He ranks climate change alongside preserving ethics and the freedom of Palestine as justice issues, and says Muslims in the West must carry it because people struggling under poverty and tyranny, like those in the Syrian village he grew up in, cannot afford to. He calls the Quran a green book full of creation and diversity, describes the Prophet's closeness to nature, the sapling hadith and the instruction not to burn trees or kill animals in war, and reads Az-Zalzalah as the earth, a mother, being commanded to testify about what we did on her. He then explains the greenhouse effect and temperature data, suspects vested interests behind denial, and names overconsumption as the cause individuals can control, noting the power of youth-led activism. In the second khutbah he argues that even selfishness should move people, and gives four steps: learn the basics, talk about it, reduce consumption, and engage in policy, teaching children so the earth does not testify against them.

outline.heading: Opening
Adam created to be a steward
outline.gist: The first verse after Al-Baqarah's introduction declares a steward on earth before Adam's creation, so his life on earth was his destiny, not only the result of a mistake.

outline.heading: A first-tier justice issue
outline.gist: A century ago this khutbah would be unnecessary; climate belongs with preserving Muslim ethics and the freedom of Palestine as a main justice issue, not a secondary one.

outline.heading: The poor cannot afford to care
outline.gist: Where people chase bread under tyranny, a sheikh raising this would be mocked; it is a luxury for them, so Muslims in the West must carry it.

outline.heading: Stewardship is tied to this earth
outline.gist: Allah said a steward on earth: we serve Him through caring for the earth, and once it is gone that role ends.

outline.heading: Creation placed in our service
outline.gist: Surah Ibrahim: water, crops, rivers, ships, sun, moon, night and day are all subjected to humans, blessings beyond counting, yet man is unjust and ungrateful.

outline.heading: The greenest book: Allah's diversity
outline.gist: Nearly every page speaks of creation; Fatir describes fruits, mountains, people and animals of many colours, a diversity we are slowly ruining.

outline.heading: The Prophet in tune with nature
outline.gist: He loved the wilderness and its beauty, and many hadith show him defending animals and rebuking their owners.

outline.heading: Plant the sapling
outline.gist: If the Hour comes while you hold a sapling, plant it: beyond its work ethic, he chose the image of a tree.

outline.heading: Do not burn a tree: no corruption on earth
outline.gist: Abu Bakr passed on the Prophet's charge to armies not to burn trees, flood land or kill animals; the Quran forbids spreading corruption on earth over 25 times, including ruining our habitat.

outline.heading: We come from the earth and return to it
outline.gist: Like the body, the earth is an amanah; we come from it, return to it and will be raised from it, yet we recite Az-Zalzalah without listening.

outline.heading: The earth casts us out
outline.gist: On the day the earth shakes and throws out its bodies, people ask what is wrong with her; a child wronged by its own mother is damaged almost beyond repair.

outline.heading: She speaks only because her Lord commands
outline.gist: Our mother will tell what we did on her and to each other only because Allah orders it, and every atom of good and evil will be seen; Muslims belong on the front lines.

outline.heading: His Syrian village, and the carbon footprint
outline.gist: His poor village never thought of this; we have the luxury to understand, and the carbon footprint map shows Canada large for its population.

outline.heading: The greenhouse effect
outline.gist: Greenhouse gases keep enough of the sun's warmth for life and send away harmful rays; burning coal for decades produces more heat than can escape, as the median temperature graph shows.

outline.heading: A graph no physician would call normal
outline.gist: Reading a chart like this as normal would kill patients; those profiting from burning coal may want people not to look.

outline.heading: Overconsumption is what we can control
outline.gist: We cannot shut distant factories, but we can cut our own consumption; in the EU climate topped policy concerns and about 60 percent credited youth-led protests.

outline.heading: Youth can change policy
outline.gist: Young people have the time, passion and means that those tied down by homes, children and jobs lack, and can shape future policy.

outline.heading: The most polluted cities
outline.gist: Air, plastic and ocean pollution; the cities with the worst air are in countries whose people should feel familiar.

outline.heading: The earth is fine; at least be selfish
outline.gist: The earth has survived mass extinctions and will be fine; we are the ones in danger, so if you will not be a steward, care out of self-interest.

outline.heading: Step one: learn the basics
outline.gist: Islamically this is responsibility, not selfishness; the last nine years were the warmest on record; from Purdue University's four steps, first understand what a one-degree change does.

outline.heading: Biodiversity and the balance
outline.gist: Losing biodiversity dooms us because we never survived alone; forests that look like lungs cannot keep up with coal and deforestation, and Islam is about keeping the balance.

outline.heading: Talk about it, consume less, shape policy
outline.gist: Discuss it openly, know your impact and live closer to the Prophet's minimalism, and engage in policy making because oppressed Muslims cannot.

outline.heading: We cannot be bystanders
outline.gist: Muslims in the West have the time and ability to act; teach children to care so the earth does not testify against them before Allah.

outline.heading: Outro

1uWDQNI-IWI.title: Contemporary Issues: Atheism and Doubt
1uWDQNI-IWI.one_line: Using Yaqeen Institute data, he shows Muslims' own behaviour drives doubt most and religious education reduces it most, and explains how to ground faith.
1uWDQNI-IWI.summary: Continuing his contemporary issues series, he calls doubt and atheism the leading problem after relationships, affecting every age and place, and walks through a Yaqeen Institute study of about 600 American Muslims. Its three categories are social and moral concerns, philosophical and scientific concerns, and personal trauma. The strongest driver, especially for youth, is the behaviour of visibly religious Muslims who are harsh, closed-minded and harmful, which he finds painful because Islam's morality is beautiful. He insists faith should never hang on any person, himself included. On philosophy and science he separates science from scientism, warns that unresolved cognitive dissonance pushes people to switch off their minds or invent a private religion, and gives four sources for knowing Allah: the universe, life, history and personal instinct. There will never be proof of God, only converging evidence. Trauma rose sharply as a cause after the Arab Spring, so faith must rest on stable foundations, not on one answered dua. The study found dogmatic strictness with children increases doubt while real religious education decreases it, so he returns to the command to read. He ends by saying doubt is normal but must be taken seriously and resolved through study.

outline.heading: Opening
Who began creation?
outline.gist: An-Naml verses: who began creation and provides, bring your proof, only Allah knows the unseen, and they are in doubt and blind about the Hereafter.

outline.heading: Doubt as the leading problem; the Yaqeen study
outline.gist: After weeks on relationships, doubt and atheism are the top issue; he walks through Dr. Youssef Chouhoud's Yaqeen Institute study of about 600 American Muslims, whose causes do not carry equal weight.

outline.heading: Every age, and the Arab Spring
outline.gist: Doubt affects all ages, both genders and every country; after 2010 war, death and destruction shook many people's faith.

outline.heading: Bucket one: the visibly religious who repel
outline.gist: Social and moral concerns weigh most, especially on the young: people who claim religiosity but act without compassion or open-mindedness, point fingers and call names are the number one repellent.

outline.heading: Islam's morality is beautiful
outline.gist: The study drew its causes from other faiths' research, since Muslims once held firmer; it depresses him that young Muslims feel a moral problem in a faith whose morality is profound.

outline.heading: Never attach your faith to a person
outline.gist: Do not leave Islam because some buffoon misrepresents it; faith attaches only to Allah, His Messenger and the senior companions after him, never to a flawed individual like himself.

outline.heading: Bucket two: science versus scientism
outline.gist: Scientism discards philosophy and logic, which makes no sense to him; settling the question of God's existence makes everything else fall into place.

outline.heading: Cognitive dissonance forces a choice
outline.gist: Unresolved dissonance ends with switching off the mind, which Islam never asks, or inventing a private faith; relearning religion and science properly takes years and people want microwave answers.

outline.heading: Choose a lane: four sources of knowing Allah
outline.gist: You cannot live in the grey area forever; the Quran points to the universe, life, history and personal instinct as the four sources of knowing Allah.

outline.heading: There will never be proof of God
outline.gist: Proof needs measurement within time and space, and Allah is beyond them, so whatever science proved to be God would not be God.

outline.heading: Evidence, not proof
outline.gist: Pictures of supposed miracles prove nothing; certainty comes from converging evidence, all arrows pointing one way; he recommends his Facing Disbelief series.

outline.heading: Bucket three: personal trauma
outline.gist: Once the weakest cause, trauma rose to the top after 2012 as people in the Middle East suffered oppression and death without a sound understanding of Allah.

outline.heading: Faith built on one answered dua
outline.gist: Iman resting on a single accepted dua collapses the first time an answer is delayed or replaced.

outline.heading: Build faith on the unchanging universe
outline.gist: The Quran repeatedly says look at the sun, moon, mountains and creatures; the universe is a source that never changes and its evidence is conclusive.

outline.heading: The leading cause is Muslims' own behaviour
outline.gist: The survey ranking puts self-righteous or harmful religious people at the top; the leading cause of doubt is how practising Muslims act.

outline.heading: What doubt costs
outline.gist: Doubters adhere less, belong less to the community and the ummah, and slowly drift away with their offspring, so all of us must examine what we project.

outline.heading: Lingering doubts: terrorism and extremism
outline.gist: Among doubts people still carry are terrorism and extremism, again the behaviour of Muslims; trauma he cannot remove, only support.

outline.heading: Early Muslims were magnets
outline.gist: We can fix representation: without wealth or castles, the early Muslims drew people by their ethics and brotherhood, and it was cool to be Muslim despite the dictators.

outline.heading: Dogmatism increases doubt
outline.gist: It should be an easy fix; the study found overly strict, clockwork enforcement on children produces more doubt, not less.

outline.heading: Religious education reduces it most
outline.gist: Proper religious education, with time invested in understanding rather than forced attendance or dress, was the strongest factor reducing doubt in every analysis.

outline.heading: Read: back to square one
outline.gist: Al-Alaq's first command to read in the name of the Lord who created is the answer; he points to the two articles.

outline.heading: Interlude
Doubt is normal, but you can't stay there
outline.gist: Doubt shows a working, critical mind and is no shame, but take it seriously, study proper sources, and do not live in it for life; an intellectual can live without doubt.

outline.heading: Outro

58:15.en: Allah hath prepared for them a dreadful doom. Evil indeed is that which they are wont to do

58:16.ar: ٱتَّخَذُوٓاْ أَيۡمَٰنَهُمۡ جُنَّةࣰ فَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَلَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ مُّهِينࣱ‏
58:16.en: They make a shelter of their oaths and turn (men) from the way of Allah; so theirs will be a shameful doom

58:17.ar: لَّن تُغۡنِيَ عَنۡهُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلُهُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيۡـًٔاۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
58:17.en: Their wealth and their children will avail them naught against Allah. Such are rightful owners of the Fire; they will abide therein

58:18.ar: يَوۡمَ يَبۡعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيَحۡلِفُونَ لَهُۥ كَمَا يَحۡلِفُونَ لَكُمۡ وَيَحۡسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمۡ عَلَىٰ شَيۡءٍۚ أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡكَٰذِبُونَ
58:18.en: On the day when Allah will raise them all together, then will they swear unto Him as they (now) swear unto you, and they will fancy that they have some standing. Lo! is it not they who are the liars

58:19.ar: ٱسۡتَحۡوَذَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ فَأَنسَىٰهُمۡ ذِكۡرَ ٱللَّهِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ حِزۡبُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۚ أَلَآ إِنَّ حِزۡبَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
58:19.en: The devil hath engrossed them and so hath caused them to forget remembrance of Allah. They are the devil's party. Lo! is it not the devil's party who will be the losers

58:20.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَآدُّونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ فِي ٱلۡأَذَلِّينَ
58:20.en: Lo! those who oppose Allah and His messenger, they will be among the lowest

58:21.ar: كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَغۡلِبَنَّ أَنَا۠ وَرُسُلِيٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزࣱ‏
58:21.en: Allah hath decreed: Lo! I verily shall conquer, I and My messengers. Lo! Allah is Strong, Almighty

58:22.ar: لَّا تَجِدُ قَوۡمࣰ ا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ يُوَآدُّونَ مَنۡ حَآدَّ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَلَوۡ كَانُوٓاْ ءَابَآءَهُمۡ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءَهُمۡ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنَهُمۡ أَوۡ عَشِيرَتَهُمۡۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ كَتَبَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ وَأَيَّدَهُم بِرُوحࣲ مِّنۡهُۖ وَيُدۡخِلُهُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ رَضِيَ ٱللَّهُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَرَضُواْ عَنۡهُۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ حِزۡبُ ٱللَّهِۚ أَلَآ إِنَّ حِزۡبَ ٱللَّهِ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
58:22.en: Thou wilt not find folk who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His messenger, even though they be their fathers or their sons or their brethren or their clan. As for such, He hath written faith upon their hearts and hath strengthened them with a Spirit from Him, and He will bring them into Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide. Allah is well pleased with them, and they are well pleased with Him. They are Allah's party. Lo! is it not Allah's party who are the successful

3:77.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَشۡتَرُونَ بِعَهۡدِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَيۡمَٰنِهِمۡ ثَمَنࣰ ا قَلِيلًا أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَا خَلَٰقَ لَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَلَا يَنظُرُ إِلَيۡهِمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
3:77.en: Lo! those who purchase a small gain at the cost of Allah's covenant and their oaths, they have no portion in the Hereafter. Allah will neither speak to them nor look upon them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He make them grow. Theirs will be a painful doom

33:20.ar: يَحۡسَبُونَ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابَ لَمۡ يَذۡهَبُواْۖ وَإِن يَأۡتِ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابُ يَوَدُّواْ لَوۡ أَنَّهُم بَادُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَعۡرَابِ يَسۡـَٔلُونَ عَنۡ أَنۢبَآئِكُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ كَانُواْ فِيكُم مَّا قَٰتَلُوٓاْ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
33:20.en: They hold that the clans have not retired (for good); and if the clans should advance (again), they would fain be in the desert with the wandering Arabs, asking for the news of you; and if they were among you, they would not give battle, save a little

m_URmEFJfOs.title: Sunday Tafseer: Surat Al-Mujadilah, Part 4 (Verses 14-22)
m_URmEFJfOs.one_line: The closing passage of Mujadilah: belonging to the ummah is the strongest bond, and divided loyalty leads to self-deception and loss.
m_URmEFJfOs.summary: He sums up the final passage of Mujadilah in one line: no bond is stronger for a Muslim than Islam. This is not about violence; it means your loyalty, wealth, volunteer time and causes go first to the Muslim community, not because Muslim blood is superior but because neglecting fellow Muslims says another bond matters more. You cannot stand outside the community criticizing 'them'; it is your ship, so get in the mud and champion your ideas. Verse fourteen observes a recurring phenomenon of people who accepted Islam but kept their belonging elsewhere and swore otherwise; since belonging cannot be checked, the verses ask each person whether they carry the deen or are carried by it. Wealth and children will not make anyone free of need before Allah. Three heavy verses follow because losing the sense of ummah threatens the passing of faith to future generations. He then explains how people swear to Allah on the Day of Judgment believing their own lie: without the ummah's checks, identity erodes, the social mask becomes the self, and uncorrected early lies become normalized. Shaytan's overpowering means forgetting Allah, not possession. Verse twenty-two describes believers whose loyalty to Allah outranks even family; being Muslim first protects family and nation and opposes oppression.

outline.heading: Why a slow, comprehensive tafsir
outline.gist: Surah summaries and thematic series have their place, but people need help knowing what to do with verses they already know.

outline.heading: The cluster and a Muslim community within Canada
outline.gist: The juz organizes Muslim relationships, which a community seeking to keep its identity and values in Canadian society needs.

outline.heading: Bottom line: no bond is stronger than Islam
outline.gist: After oppression, secret counsel, welcoming everyone and respecting leaders, the surah ends with allegiance.

outline.heading: Not a call to violence: an ideology worth living for
outline.gist: Any ideology not worth living and dying for is not worth belonging to; you take Islam as a whole.

outline.heading: What it means in practice: priorities of wealth and time
outline.gist: Give first to causes affecting Muslims, not because Muslim blood is superior but because neglecting them disrespects that bond.

outline.heading: You cannot isolate yourself from the community
outline.gist: Muslims are not flawless, but this is your ship: we sail or sink together.

outline.heading: Do not bring ideas, champion them
outline.gist: Gather people, fundraise and move your idea forward yourself.

outline.heading: Those who serve also have lives
outline.gist: No one is appointed; everyone has a role, and he will step aside for someone more qualified.

outline.heading: Saying they instead of we
outline.gist: Muslims who speak of Muslims as 'they' have placed themselves in another group.

outline.heading: Recitation note: ghunnah and colour-coded mushafs
outline.gist: When the noon and meem carry two counts, and how a colour-coded mushaf helps.

outline.heading: Interlude
Have you not seen: a Madinan way of provoking observation
outline.gist: The phrase points the Prophet to problems in his reality; Makkan surahs dealing with fundamentals rarely use it.

outline.heading: Observing a recurring phenomenon
outline.gist: The added preposition turns seeing people into observing something that keeps happening.

outline.heading: Tawalla: social and religious belonging, not politics
outline.gist: Wala' here is about alliance and belonging within the community; politics comes in later surahs.

outline.heading: Allied with those under wrath: neither of you nor of them
outline.gist: New Muslims kept loyalty to tribes and friends who fought Islam or refused its call.

outline.heading: Swearing falsely: Islam without belonging
outline.gist: They took the theology they liked but refused to help, pay zakat or share the community's problems, then swore otherwise.

outline.heading: When practice lapses, belonging lapses too
outline.gist: The loss in not practicing is not only rituals but the sense of belonging.

outline.heading: Oaths as a shield: belonging cannot be audited
outline.gist: No one can hold another accountable for where they belong; Allah will.

outline.heading: Do you carry the deen or does it carry you?
outline.gist: There is only one acceptable place: on the ground pushing forward within your capacity.

outline.heading: Dead weight in the ummah
outline.gist: Muslims on paper who need care but never participate or admit shortcomings explain the severity of these verses.

outline.heading: Interlude
Wealth and children will not make them free of need
outline.gist: Ghina means not needing anything; no empire of wealth or kin removes our need of Allah on that day.

outline.heading: Hoping Allah will simply look at you
outline.gist: The difference between being glanced at with compassion and being ignored is survival.

outline.heading: Three verses of severity: hit the brakes
outline.gist: Rarely does the Quran spend three verses on one behaviour's punishment; ask whether you have thought your belonging through.

outline.heading: Why it matters: passing the faith to future generations
outline.gist: Muslims push back disbelief so that generation after generation can know Allah; broken belonging ends that story.

outline.heading: A Muslim who does not belong
outline.gist: Losing the sense of ummah normalizes something incomprehensible; Islam is what Allah wants it to be, not what we want.

outline.heading: The answer is to strengthen bonds, not walk away
outline.gist: Strengthen the masajid and people's bonds with them.

outline.heading: Like and love are different
outline.gist: You do not have to like everyone in your family to love and stand by them; the ummah is the family Allah chose for you.

outline.heading: Swearing to Allah as they swore to you
outline.gist: On Judgment Day they lie to Allah and think they are onto something: they believe their own lie.

outline.heading: Losing identity breeds self-deception
outline.gist: Without belonging you no longer know who you are and can be convinced of what is false, a known psychological defence.

outline.heading: Taking off the mask when alone
outline.gist: Everyone wears a social mask; can you take it off at home and hold yourself accountable?

outline.heading: The ummah keeps you in check
outline.gist: Belonging means others push you back to what is right.

outline.heading: People living inside their own illusion
outline.gist: Everyone knows the truth but them, and no one dares say it.

outline.heading: An early lie left unfixed becomes the truth to you
outline.gist: A mistake ignored because it was convenient gets normalized and forgotten until you stand before Allah defending it.

outline.heading: Do it while you are young
outline.gist: Confronting twenty years of self-deception is far harder than confronting two.

outline.heading: Interlude
Recitation note: the six-count madd and the silent alif
outline.gist: The oval sign over an alif means it is dropped when reading on and pronounced when stopping, in this reading.

outline.heading: Shaytan has overpowered them: not possession
outline.gist: Istahwadha means surrounding from every side through whispering; they need guidance and self-accountability, not exorcism.

outline.heading: Forgetting Allah makes the mask possible
outline.gist: If you remember Allah, keeping up a front before Him is pointless; honesty with yourself is what saves.

outline.heading: Hizb: a group, not a political party
outline.gist: Like the Ahzab, a group united by one goal; the party of Shaytan are the losers.

outline.heading: Those who defy Allah will be among the most humiliated
outline.gist: This echoes verse five, the second time in the surah.

outline.heading: Allah has decreed: I and My messengers will prevail
outline.gist: Success belongs to those who choose to belong to Allah and His Prophet's group.

outline.heading: The logic of the passage
outline.gist: Choosing the wrong belonging leads to losing yourself and ending in the losing group.

outline.heading: Recitation note: two six-count madds in one verse
outline.gist: A rare pattern that appears in recitation contests.

outline.heading: No believing people give their loyalty to those who oppose Allah
outline.gist: Mawaddah here means belonging and allegiance, even when the opponents are fathers, sons, brothers or tribe.

outline.heading: The story of a companion and his father: not authentic
outline.gist: He mentions the reported occasion only to note it lacks an authentic chain and does not fit the history; the verse is general.

outline.heading: Kinship matters, but Islam's bond comes first
outline.gist: Keeping family ties is vital, yet we are always Muslim first.

outline.heading: Muslim first protects everything else
outline.gist: Being Muslim first means never betraying dependents and refusing oppression; those who dislike that expose themselves, and we must not water down our identity.

outline.heading: Faith written in their hearts and a spirit from Him
outline.gist: Belonging is evidence of iman; scholars do not know exactly what the spirit is, but Allah strengthens those who choose this.

outline.heading: Mutual pleasure and the party of Allah
outline.gist: Allah is pleased with them and they with Him; the party of Allah succeeds, with no political meaning.

24:19.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحِبُّونَ أَن تَشِيعَ ٱلۡفَٰحِشَةُ فِي ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
24:19.en: Lo! those who love that slander should be spread concerning those who believe, theirs will be a painful punishment in the world and the Hereafter. Allah knoweth. Ye know not

17:32.ar: وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلزِّنَىٰٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فَٰحِشَةࣰ وَسَآءَ سَبِيلࣰ ا
17:32.en: And come not near unto adultery. Lo! it is an abomination and an evil way

7:175.ar: وَٱتۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَبَأَ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا فَٱنسَلَخَ مِنۡهَا فَأَتۡبَعَهُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡغَاوِينَ
7:175.en: Recite unto them the tale of him to whom We gave Our revelations, but he sloughed them off, so Satan overtook him and he became of those who lead astray

7:176.ar: وَلَوۡ شِئۡنَا لَرَفَعۡنَٰهُ بِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّهُۥٓ أَخۡلَدَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُۚ فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡكَلۡبِ إِن تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡهِ يَلۡهَثۡ أَوۡ تَتۡرُكۡهُ يَلۡهَثۚ ذَّٰلِكَ مَثَلُ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَاۚ فَٱقۡصُصِ ٱلۡقَصَصَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
7:176.en: And had We willed We could have raised him by their means, but he clung to the earth and followed his own lust. Therefor his likeness is as the likeness of a dog: if thou attackest him he panteth with his tongue out, and if thou leavest him he panteth with his tongue out. Such is the likeness of the people who deny Our revelations. Narrate unto them the history (of the men of old), that haply they may take thought

24:30.ar: قُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ وَيَحۡفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَزۡكَىٰ لَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا يَصۡنَعُونَ
24:30.en: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and be modest. That is purer for them. Lo! Allah is aware of what they do

24:31.ar: وَقُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَغۡضُضۡنَ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحۡفَظۡنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَاۖ وَلۡيَضۡرِبۡنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّۖ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوۡ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ ٱلتَّٰبِعِينَ غَيۡرِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡإِرۡبَةِ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ أَوِ ٱلطِّفۡلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوۡرَٰتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِۖ وَلَا يَضۡرِبۡنَ بِأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعۡلَمَ مَا يُخۡفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّۚ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
24:31.en: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and be modest, and to display of their adornment only that which is apparent, and to draw their veils over their bosoms, and not to reveal their adornment save to their own husbands or fathers or husbands' fathers, or their sons or their husbands' sons, or their brothers or their brothers' sons or sisters' sons, or their women, or their slaves, or male attendants who lack vigour, or children who know naught of women's nakedness. And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment. And turn unto Allah together, O believers, in order that ye may succeed

_qDz12D9rkY.title: Contemporary Issues: Sexual Overexposure
_qDz12D9rkY.one_line: Unprecedented sexual exposure and pornography are damaging individuals and marriages; five points on the gaze, pornography, the narrative, Islam's system and seeking help.
_qDz12D9rkY.summary: He opens with the An-Nur verse threatening those who love to see indecency spread, noting that Allah knows what people then could not imagine. A phone now shows more obscenity in minutes than a grandfather saw in a lifetime, and he cites research on anxiety, depression and eating disorders in girls, aggression in boys, early first exposure and divorces linked to pornography. Allah forbids only what harms, some social damage reaches a point of no return, and the command not to even approach zina must be taken seriously. Al-A'raf's image of the man who sheds guidance, follows his desires and pants like a dog shows how grave this is. His five points: lowering the gaze is a skill, an act of worship and a habit parents must teach and model; pornography conditions the brain so real spouses disappoint and the industry exploits the vulnerable; Muslims must reclaim the narrative that this is unacceptable rather than normal; Islam offers a whole system of modesty, hijab and haya that cannot be cherry-picked, where dress invites respect rather than desire; and anyone struggling should seek help, while parents supervise devices and educate their children themselves.

outline.heading: Opening
Those who love indecency to spread
outline.gist: An-Nur verse promising severe punishment to those who love indecency to spread; its ending, Allah knows and you do not, hints at a scale no one then could imagine; the new topic in the contemporary issues series.

outline.heading: More in four minutes than a grandfather's lifetime
outline.gist: A phone exposes you to more obscenity in minutes than a grandfather met in his whole life; thinking this leaves the psyche, sexuality and relationships untouched is naive.

outline.heading: What the research shows
outline.gist: Anxiety, depression, low self-esteem and eating disorders in girls, aggression and dissatisfaction in boys; he quotes figures on near-universal consumption, a median starting age of 11, and divorces linked to it.

outline.heading: Haram because it harms, and the point of no return
outline.gist: Allah forbids nothing for the fun of it; some damage only shows generations later, and a community's mentality ruined long enough cannot be brought back.

outline.heading: Do not even approach zina
outline.gist: Al-Isra: stay as far as possible from everything that leads to zina; we think we have it under control and we do not, which is why he speaks plainly.

outline.heading: The one who shed Allah's signs
outline.gist: Al-A'raf: the man given Allah's signs who threw them off like a skin he had outgrown, and Shaytan followed him.

outline.heading: Like a dog that pants either way
outline.gist: Instead of being raised by guidance he clung to the earth and his desires, like a dog panting burdened or not; Allah unburdened us and we chose the burden, and such animal comparisons are rare and grave in the Quran.

outline.heading: Point one: lowering the gaze is worship and a skill
outline.gist: Teach it at home like salah and honesty; he reads the An-Nur command as: tell the believers the truth, and if they believe they will lower their gaze.

outline.heading: You can't teach what you don't model
outline.gist: Parents must practise it themselves, or their children will not; it is a skill learned against curiosity.

outline.heading: Look away from people's private moments
outline.gist: The gaze also covers what people do not want seen, a scene in their home or a public outburst; with practice it becomes a habit and an act of obedience.

outline.heading: Interlude
Point two: pornography by the numbers
outline.gist: He is no expert but cites 85 percent of boys aged 16 to 17 consuming it regularly and a third of consumers being women, with the self-stimulation that accompanies it.

outline.heading: Conditioning that ruins marriage
outline.gist: Years of artificially enhanced content condition the brain, so a real spouse disappoints; the young man who waited years to marry finds no satisfaction because no one warned him.

outline.heading: An exploitative industry
outline.gist: It exploits the poor, the mentally ill and the desperate, packages zina as entertainment, and its profits help explain why science says little about it.

outline.heading: Point three: reclaim the narrative
outline.gist: Muslims must say plainly that this is haram and must not be so accessible; it once took effort and embarrassment to find, now everything is sold through sex and children are fed it.

outline.heading: Sexuality is too powerful to leave open
outline.gist: Only food and drink rival this instinct; Allah built a system around something so delicate, and throwing every door open endangers everyone.

outline.heading: Point four: Islam's system, without cherry-picking
outline.gist: Allah gave a whole way of life of prohibitions and obligations that protects a community; ignoring parts of it has left some things hard to salvage.

outline.heading: Hijab: dress to invite respect
outline.gist: With hishmah, hijab and haya, both men and women dress to provoke only integrity and respect, unlike dressing to look desirable.

outline.heading: A hypersexualized culture we must not join
outline.gist: Dressing to be wanted is now normal and leaves men and women anxious about how they must look; Muslims cannot play into a culture that no longer knows pure from filthy.

outline.heading: Point five: seek help
outline.gist: No one reaches maturity at 15 and avoids this for 20 years; anyone with an addiction should seek help, even from non-Islamic resources.

outline.heading: Supervise devices; it sells
outline.gist: These cases reach him often; unsupervised devices without firewalls make exposure a matter of time, since mainstream entertainment inserts it because it sells.

outline.heading: Parents must teach their children first
outline.gist: Children must hear about sexuality from their parents before anyone else, so parents must educate themselves rather than rely on how things were a generation ago.

outline.heading: Outro

59:1.en: All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifieth Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

59:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ لِأَوَّلِ ٱلۡحَشۡرِۚ مَا ظَنَنتُمۡ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْۖ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُم مَّانِعَتُهُمۡ حُصُونُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ فَأَتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَمۡ يَحۡتَسِبُواْۖ وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلرُّعۡبَۚ يُخۡرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُم بِأَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَأَيۡدِي ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ فَٱعۡتَبِرُواْ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ
59:2.en: He it is Who hath caused those of the People of the Scripture who disbelieved to go forth from their homes unto the first exile. Ye deemed not that they would go forth, while they deemed that their strongholds would protect them from Allah. But Allah reached them from a place whereof they recked not, and cast terror in their hearts so that they ruined their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So learn a lesson, O ye who have eyes

59:3.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ أَن كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡجَلَآءَ لَعَذَّبَهُمۡ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابُ ٱلنَّارِ
59:3.en: And if Allah had not decreed migration for them, He verily would have punished them in the world, and theirs in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire

59:4.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ شَآقُّواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥۖ وَمَن يُشَآقِّ ٱللَّهَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
59:4.en: That is because they were opposed to Allah and His messenger; and whoso is opposed to Allah, (for him) verily Allah is stern in reprisal

37u7iJdbCeE.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Hashr, Part 1: Verses 1-4
37u7iJdbCeE.one_line: Al-Hashr as the surah of citizenship: the Constitution of Medina, Banu al-Nadir's betrayal and expulsion, and why citizens may never harm their own country.
37u7iJdbCeE.summary: He introduces the last four juz as a summary of the whole Quran and places Al-Hashr in a cluster about organising relationships, calling it the surah of citizenship. The Prophet built a diverse society around an idea and gave Medina a constitution guaranteeing every group its faith, land and wealth in return for loyalty. When a Jewish tribe, coordinating with the hypocrites and Quraysh, plotted to drop a boulder on the Prophet while he visited to borrow blood money, then refused justice and fortified itself, the contract was broken. He explains why surahs open with tasbih: Allah establishes who He is before giving law, and as the Unfathomable and Wise He can command what we do not yet understand. He argues later generations can understand the Quran more deeply than its first hearers because they see its history whole. Verse 2 yields a firm rule: a citizen may never harm his country or fellow citizens, as Muslims in Mecca never assassinated anyone or broke an idol. The Muslims thought the fortified tribe unbeatable, a lesson on inferiority complexes, yet Allah cast terror into its heart during a siege the weak Muslims could not have sustained. His central exhortation is to pour your soul into whatever you do. Verses 3-4 explain that exile spared bloodshed and that the cause was betraying Allah and His Messenger.

outline.heading: The last four juz summarise the Quran
outline.gist: The Mufassal surahs condense the concepts of the first twenty-six juz, so knowing them gives nearly everything a Muslim needs.

outline.heading: The previous cluster: a chain of choices
outline.gist: Each surah from the earlier cluster poses a choice: truth or falsehood, purpose or aimlessness, gratitude or loss.

outline.heading: This cluster organises relationships
outline.gist: Late Medinan surahs; Al-Mujadalah covered relations among individual Muslims and with their leaders.

outline.heading: A society united by an idea, not lineage
outline.gist: The Prophet brought together people of different backgrounds, and many groups with differing goals formed within it.

outline.heading: The surah of citizenship
outline.gist: Al-Hashr defines belonging to a larger group and how its sub-groups relate, even across belief systems.

outline.heading: Medina's growing power and threats to the Prophet
outline.gist: By the fourth year after Badr and Uhud, tribes feared him; he survived many assassination attempts.

outline.heading: The Constitution of Medina
outline.gist: An underrated document guaranteeing each group its religion, land and wealth in return for keeping the city safe or at least not opposing it.

outline.heading: The Jewish tribes sign, expecting it not to last
outline.gist: Unlike conquerors who humiliated the powerful, he offered partnership; they signed believing the Muslims would soon fall, then Badr happened.

outline.heading: Setbacks that strengthen show what will survive
outline.gist: Uhud made Muslims stronger, which worried their enemies more; Medina held Aws, Khazraj, hypocrites and pagans who were never forced to convert.

outline.heading: Why people joined: the novelty of Medina
outline.gist: Some embraced Islam to ride a popular wave; the new community, its masjid and its constitution were the talk of Arabia.

outline.heading: From client status to equal citizenship
outline.gist: Cities were single tribes with attached clients; the constitution made each group an equal party.

outline.heading: The Prophet's visits to the tribes
outline.gist: He visited the sick, accepted invitations and included the tribes in decisions.

outline.heading: Banu al-Nadir: blood money for an accidental killing
outline.gist: A Muslim mistakenly killed two allies; the Prophet chose to pay their blood money himself and went to borrow it.

outline.heading: Banu al-Nadir: the boulder plot
outline.gist: They placed a man on a roof to drop a boulder on him; warned by Jibril, he left by another route and confronted their elders.

outline.heading: Banu al-Nadir: refusing justice and fortifying
outline.gist: Promised support by Ibn Ubayy and others, they refused to hand over the culprit and prepared for war; the surah tells the story from the end.

outline.heading: Interlude
Tajweed: lengthening counts in the first verse
outline.gist: A shaddah on nun or mim always takes two counts; the verse is good practice for timing.

outline.heading: Everything exalts Allah
outline.gist: Tasbih means exalting and frequent remembrance; all things glorify Him actively and by their very existence.

outline.heading: Why law-giving surahs open with tasbih
outline.gist: Before organising behaviour, Allah establishes who He is so that people listen, as He uses oaths elsewhere.

outline.heading: The Unfathomable and the Wise
outline.gist: A god you could fully comprehend would not be God; His wisdom guarantees commands we do not yet understand are for our good.

outline.heading: Later generations can understand the Quran more deeply
outline.gist: Centuries later we see the Prophet's life and its effects across history, revealing precision the first generation could not survey.

outline.heading: No one knows an iconic moment while living it
outline.gist: Like players in a famous game or our own turning points, the significance becomes clear only in hindsight.

outline.heading: Ubayy ibn Ka'b named by Allah, and our duty to exceed
outline.gist: The companions did not know they were part of the story; they would be disappointed if we did not understand more than they did.

outline.heading: Expelled at the first gathering
outline.gist: Al-Hashr means gathering or removal; those who betray the community break the law and must leave.

outline.heading: Citizens may never harm their own country
outline.gist: No circumstance permits a Muslim citizen to harm his country or fellow citizens; if he cannot change its policies he may leave.

outline.heading: Mecca: no assassinations, no broken idols
outline.gist: For thirteen years Muslims had no permission to fight and never smashed an idol; Umar's brawl on his first day was before he learned the rule.

outline.heading: 'You did not think they would leave'
outline.gist: Their long settlement, walls and wealth made Muslims assume they were untouchable.

outline.heading: Inferiority complexes in Muslim communities
outline.gist: Unfounded assumptions breed inferiority; self-criticism is needed, but confidence and a strong identity are part of being Muslim.

outline.heading: Fortresses cannot hold back Allah
outline.gist: They thought their castles protected them from Allah, but He came from where they did not expect.

outline.heading: Banu al-Nadir: the weakness of the besieging Muslims
outline.gist: Fewer than fifteen hundred, poor, recently ill in Medina's climate; Bilal longed for Mecca.

outline.heading: Banu al-Nadir: the siege and the terror
outline.gist: Their stores could outlast Medina for years, yet panic spread until the people forced their leaders to surrender.

outline.heading: Pour your soul into whatever you do
outline.gist: The believers brought their full best though it was little; give everything to work and worship, not only to leisure.

outline.heading: Ruining their homes with their own hands
outline.gist: Allah's terror ended it within days; take heed, those with insight: give your best and know betrayal leads to exile.

outline.heading: Interlude
Exile instead of bloodshed
outline.gist: Had Allah not decreed exile, war would have punished everyone; they escaped worldly punishment but face the Hereafter.

outline.heading: Recap of the passage
outline.gist: Expelled at the first gathering despite their confidence, fear overtook them and exile spared bloodshed.

outline.heading: Shaqq: betraying Allah and His Messenger
outline.gist: Opposing what you know is right tears the fabric of truth, and Allah's punishment for it is severe.

outline.heading: Betrayal breaks the contract of citizenship
outline.gist: Loyalty to the groups within the community is part of loyalty to Allah; the Prophet had no wish to expel anyone.

outline.heading: Outro

38:17.ar: ٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱذۡكُرۡ عَبۡدَنَا دَاوُۥدَ ذَا ٱلۡأَيۡدِۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
38:17.en: Bear with what they say, and remember Our bondman David, lord of might, Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (toward Allah)

38:18.ar: إِنَّا سَخَّرۡنَا ٱلۡجِبَالَ مَعَهُۥ يُسَبِّحۡنَ بِٱلۡعَشِيِّ وَٱلۡإِشۡرَاقِ
38:18.en: Lo! We subdued the hills to hymn the praises (of their Lord) with him at nightfall and sunrise

38:19.en: And the birds assembled; all were turning unto Him

38:20.ar: وَشَدَدۡنَا مُلۡكَهُۥ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَفَصۡلَ ٱلۡخِطَابِ
38:20.en: We made his kingdom strong and gave him wisdom and decisive speech

38:21.ar: ۞وَهَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ نَبَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَصۡمِ إِذۡ تَسَوَّرُواْ ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ
38:21.en: And hath the story of the litigants come unto thee? How they climbed the wall into the royal chamber

38:22.ar: إِذۡ دَخَلُواْ عَلَىٰ دَاوُۥدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنۡهُمۡۖ قَالُواْ لَا تَخَفۡۖ خَصۡمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعۡضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تُشۡطِطۡ وَٱهۡدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ
38:22.en: How they burst in upon David, and he was afraid of them. They said: Be not afraid! (We are) two litigants, one of whom hath wronged the other, therefor judge aright between us; be not unjust; and show us the fair way

38:23.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَآ أَخِي لَهُۥ تِسۡعࣱ وَتِسۡعُونَ نَعۡجَةࣰ وَلِيَ نَعۡجَةࣱ وَٰحِدَةࣱ فَقَالَ أَكۡفِلۡنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِي فِي ٱلۡخِطَابِ
38:23.en: Lo! this my brother hath ninety and nine ewes while I had one ewe; and he said: Entrust it to me, and he conquered me in speech

38:24.ar: قَالَ لَقَدۡ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعۡجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦۖ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبۡغِي بَعۡضُهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَقَلِيلࣱ مَّا هُمۡۗ وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّٰهُ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّۤ رَاكِعࣰ اۤ وَأَنَابَ۩
38:24.en: (David) said: He hath wronged thee in demanding thine ewe in addition to his ewes, and lo! many partners oppress one another, save such as believe and do good works, and they are few. And David guessed that We had tried him, and he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he bowed himself and fell down prostrate and repented

38:25.ar: فَغَفَرۡنَا لَهُۥ ذَٰلِكَۖ وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلۡفَىٰ وَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:25.en: So We forgave him that; and lo! he had access to Our presence and a happy journey's end

eEe692d9S3I.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Sad, the Story of Dawud and the Two Litigants (38:17-25)
eEe692d9S3I.one_line: Dawud as the model of the awwab: a powerful, wise king who turns back to Allah the moment he sees his own mistake.
eEe692d9S3I.summary: Surat Sad teaches that obedience to Allah is impossible without the ability to return to the truth once you realise you have left it, while the disbelievers are held back by pride and stubborn opposition. Allah consoles the Prophet with the example of Dawud: strong, gifted, a king, judge, soldier, inventor and reciter whose voice made mountains and birds glorify with him, and above all awwab, one who returns often. He dwells on 'decisive speech', arguing that the ummah has lost agreed constants: everyone now issues religious opinions, settled matters like Palestine and the rejection of homosexuality are being reopened, and principles are traded away the way Quraysh tried to bargain with the Prophet. He then tells the story of the two litigants who climbed into Dawud's prayer chamber, firmly rejecting the Israelite account involving Uriah's wife and reading the verses at face value. Dawud's slip was ruling after hearing only one side. Despite their rudeness he did not point to their faults; he immediately sought forgiveness and bowed. He asks listeners to own their own mistakes, take religion from qualified teachers, and keep the shared fundamentals clear.

outline.heading: The axis of Surat Sad: obedience means returning to the truth
outline.gist: Within the group of surahs from Al-Ahzab to Az-Zumar on submission, Sad argues that no one truly obeys Allah unless he can return to the truth when he drifts from it, as the prophets and great companions did.

outline.heading: Pride and stubborn opposition behind disbelief
outline.gist: Recap of the opening: the disbelievers know the truth but pride ('izzah) and shiqaq keep them on falsehood; people justify small wrongs, and insisting on small falsehoods leads to bigger ones.

outline.heading: Be patient and remember Our servant Dawud
outline.gist: The believer follows the truth whether it suits him or not; Allah tells the Prophet to bear the mockery and learn from Dawud.

outline.heading: One verse ties the story to the opening
outline.gist: Ending one topic and opening a new story in the same verse links Dawud's story to the theme of denying clear truth.

outline.heading: Denial (takdhib) is worse than disbelief
outline.gist: Takdhib only describes someone to whom the truth became clear and who rejected it anyway, like Abu Jahl.

outline.heading: Musaylimah's followers knew he was a liar
outline.gist: Despite the Quran's challenge, some followed Musaylimah out of tribal loyalty, preferring a liar of Rabi'ah to a truthful man of Mudar; unchecked, such wrongs pile up and veil the heart.

outline.heading: Admitting you were wrong is painful
outline.gist: Everyone finds it hard, spouses especially, but the lover of truth returns at once, as Umar did when corrected on the minbar.

outline.heading: Possessor of strength: Dawud's many roles
outline.gist: Dhal-ayd means power and capability: king, commander, judge, ironworker and inventor, father and reciter with a voice the Prophet compared to Abu Musa's.

outline.heading: The prayer and fasting of Dawud
outline.gist: The Prophet named Dawud's night prayer and alternate-day fast as the best, showing his special standing.

outline.heading: Awwab: the one who returns again and again
outline.gist: The key word of the surah: not just tawwab but someone who comes back quickly every time and never persists in error.

outline.heading: Reciting al-ishraq and the qalqalah endings
outline.gist: Tajweed notes: give the ra' of al-ishraq its heaviness and bounce the qalqalah letters that end most verses on this page.

outline.heading: Allah subjected creation to weak man
outline.gist: Taskhir: mountains for Dawud, and the sky, seas, rivers, sun and moon for all people, out of Allah's honour for humanity.

outline.heading: What tasbih means: repetition and remembrance
outline.gist: The root carries repetition, like swimming; Dawud recited the Psalms at evening and sunrise and the mountains and flocking birds joined him.

outline.heading: Everything glorifies Allah in its own way
outline.gist: The mountains' tasbih need not be speech; every creature prays and glorifies in a manner we do not understand.

outline.heading: Dawud gathered all creatures in worship and a firm kingdom
outline.gist: He united not only people but creation in praising Allah, and Allah made his kingdom strong and cohesive.

outline.heading: Kings without wisdom drive people from their homes
outline.gist: Power without wisdom ruins nations and leaves people as exiles far from the lands of their grandfathers.

outline.heading: Decisive speech: the ummah lost its authoritative voice
outline.gist: Everyone now speaks on religion without knowledge; the deen is inherited knowledge passed down from scholars, not a hobby for the bored.

outline.heading: A vast ummah needs shared constants
outline.gist: Across cultures and centuries Muslims can differ on details but must agree on tawhid, the Quran, the Sunnah and rejecting shirk and oppression.

outline.heading: Palestine is not open to debate
outline.gist: He grew up never hearing Muslims question the cause of Al-Aqsa and now hears its sanctity bargained over.

outline.heading: Negotiation is fine, compromising principles is not
outline.gist: Quraysh offered to alternate worship yearly or accept Islam without sitting with Bilal and Ammar; the deen is accepted as it is, not one letter changed.

outline.heading: Holding firm on sexual morality
outline.gist: Muslims still reject what is imposed through media and schools, but weak shared principles risk someone opening the door; he cites Lut's people.

outline.heading: Shaytan's step-by-step erosion
outline.gist: Values of honesty, chastity and modesty were not negotiable ten years ago; Iblis moved people gradually.

outline.heading: Do not weaken the decisive word
outline.gist: Do not speak without knowledge, learn from a teacher, and do not turn a legitimately disputed issue into a fundamental that splits the ummah.

outline.heading: Decisive speech as judging between people
outline.gist: The commentators also read it as Dawud's role as judge who settles disputes.

outline.heading: The litigants climb into the mihrab
outline.gist: The story begins: two men scale the wall of his prayer chamber and frighten him.

outline.heading: Reciting tushtit: the strongest and weakest letters
outline.gist: Keep the ta' light before the double ta'; ta' carries every strong quality and fa' every weak one, which is why even 'uff' to parents is forbidden.

outline.heading: 'Has the news reached you?': a Quranic way to draw attention
outline.gist: The style builds anticipation for a story the Prophet had not heard.

outline.heading: Dawud's set time for private worship
outline.gist: Busy king and judge, he kept a weekly time in his mihrab; all his roles were worship but he wanted dedicated devotion.

outline.heading: Rituals matter: against 'just worship with your heart'
outline.gist: Allah commanded five prayers a day; dismissing outward rites is as wrong as harshness about them. Tasawwur means climbing over the wall.

outline.heading: Barging in on a man at prayer, and the meaning of faza'
outline.gist: They neither knocked nor waited; his alarm is surprise and displeasure, not cowardice, like the Prophet rushing out at a noise in Madinah.

outline.heading: Transgression and the rejection of oppression
outline.gist: Baghy and zulm are condemned in every form; injustice is the opposite of truth and justice. Telling a judge to be fair is permitted.

outline.heading: Their rudeness and Dawud's patience
outline.gist: Probably two angels, they intruded, frightened him and lectured him on fairness, yet he neither punished nor dismissed them.

outline.heading: Only a father wants you to surpass him
outline.gist: Only his son Sulayman exceeded Dawud's kingdom; a father, and a sheikh who understands the deen, wants his student to surpass him.

outline.heading: The ninety-nine ewes and the single ewe
outline.gist: Recitation of the case and Dawud's ruling, with grammar notes on the numbers.

outline.heading: The prostration in Surat Sad
outline.gist: Hanafis and Malikis prostrate here, Shafi'is and Hanbalis largely do not; scholars differ whether it is a recitation or a gratitude prostration.

outline.heading: 'Give her to me' and overpowering speech
outline.gist: One brother with ninety-nine ewes pressured his poor brother into handing over his only one.

outline.heading: The Israelite account of Uriah's wife
outline.gist: The Bible's story of Dawud sending Uriah to die to marry his wife is a distortion rejected by all scholars.

outline.heading: Rejecting the softer divorce version and reading at face value
outline.gist: Even the version Ibn Ashur accepted, that Dawud asked a man to divorce his wife, has no basis and contradicts Allah's praise; the plain story makes more sense.

outline.heading: Distorted scripture invites ridicule
outline.gist: By corrupting Dawud's story the People of the Book handed atheists material to mock their religion.

outline.heading: Partners often wrong each other
outline.gist: Dawud added a general rule: business partners commonly transgress except those who believe and do good, and they are few.

outline.heading: Dawud's slip: ruling after hearing one side
outline.gist: Following Abu Bakr al-Jaza'iri rather than the view that he suspected them, the mistake was judging before hearing the other party, as Shurayh warned.

outline.heading: He repented at once despite their faults
outline.gist: They intruded and insulted him, yet he did not make excuses; he sought forgiveness, bowed and turned back immediately.

outline.heading: You answer for your own mistakes, not other people's
outline.gist: On Judgment Day you will not be asked about others; do not point at the ummah's failures, account for your own.

outline.heading: 'So We forgave him that': Allah counted it a mistake
outline.gist: A small slip in a sea of good still required istighfar, and Allah rewarded it with nearness and a good return.

outline.heading: Outro
